target_customer: Defense customers, such as militaries buying low cost air defense interceptors against cheap drones and munitions
problem: Cheap drones and munitions are countered with very expensive interceptors; the company aims to build low cost counter weapon systems at production scale.
business_model: Hardware sales to defense customers, manufacturing at automotive style scale
product_category: Defense hardware, low cost missile based interceptors for air defense

founders.name: Jack Oswald
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. Shail Giroux is named COO and co-founder in Axios and SiliconANGLE coverage but not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Anduril
competitors.what: Defense technology company; teamed with Epirus on a counter drone system with its Lattice software for a Marine Corps demonstration
competitors.traction_then: Large defense contractor with counter drone work

competitors.name: Epirus
competitors.what: High power microwave counter drone system (Leonidas)

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing and flight testing missile interceptors in house, with hardware and software developed internally and multiple flight tests per month per press.

defensibility.rationale: Defense procurement and manufacturing scale are hard barriers, and the company has senior military advisers, but Anduril and others also build interceptors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition by 2026; Singularity raised an independent Series A in July 2026.

market_need_then: Cheap drones threatened expensive air defense economics; Axios and others describe demand for low cost interceptors. Interceptors were still in development at the 2026 launch, with no public specifications.

branding.domain_note: Uses singularityus.com, with legal name Singularity Defense Corp in trade press.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, for example Build to Protect People and answering humanity's call

branding.community_and_virality: Broad press at the July 2026 stealth exit (Axios, SiliconANGLE, Defense Daily, Dot LA); no merch or fan evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic name shared with many companies, with coverage driven by the funding round rather than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Singularity stayed in stealth after Summer 2023 and then emerged in July 2026 with an 80 million dollar Series A at a reported 400 million dollar valuation led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with a team above 65 people. A propulsion engineer founder with SpaceX and Impulse experience and demand for cheap interceptors helped. Products are not yet publicly specified, so delivery risk remains.
notes: Total raised conflicts across aggregators (FundedIQ $80M, Caplight $137M), so coverage is partial because earlier funding, including YC's standard deal, is not itemised. Sources disagree on HQ (Los Angeles vs El Segundo). The YC page lists only Jack Oswald; COO Shail Giroux is named in press. Competitors are as of July 2023 from Defense One, whose article concerns the Anduril and Epirus teaming; other counter drone sources found were 2025 to 2026 and are excluded.
